sections.html:
Derby is a city in Sedgwick County and the largest suburb of Wichita, lying south of the city next to McConnell Air Force Base. Derby had 25,625 people in 2020 and an estimated 26,606 in July 2025, spread over about 9.6 square miles. Textron Aviation and other aircraft makers, Derby Public Schools and McConnell are the main employers.

Because McConnell is a major Air Force hub, plenty of sellers have orders with a fixed report date. A listing that could take months may simply not fit.

The county values Derby parcels and the city issues permits. Knowing which office owns which question saves calls.

Derby Public Schools, USD 260, serves Derby, McConnell Air Force Base, the Oaklawn Improvement District and some southern parts of Wichita. So an address that says Wichita may still be in Derby's district. Besides elementary schools, USD 260 operates a sixth grade center, a middle school, a high school and an alternative high school, and Wineteer Elementary serves McConnell family housing.

Haysville USD 261, Mulvane USD 263, Goddard USD 265 and Andover USD 385 sit next door, so a house near a boundary deserves a check. Look up the district for your own address before telling a buyer about schools.

Derby wants a permit for a long list of projects, and contractors need a city license. Typical permit jobs:

  • Fences, decks, garages, pools, sheds, pergolas, gazebos and outdoor kitchens.
  • Most electrical, plumbing and heating or air conditioning work.
  • Driveway approaches, retaining walls, sprinkler systems and wells.
  • Roofing and siding replacement over 400 square feet.
  • Anything built in a flood plain, which also needs a Flood Plain Development Permit.

Inspections catch problems such as an improperly installed water heater, faulty wiring or a deck built below code. Wondering if a contractor holds a city license? Call 788-6632 or email permits@derbyweb.com. Inspections must be requested 24 hours ahead on the residential permit form.

A basement finished or deck added by an earlier owner with no permit can draw questions from a buyer's inspector. Requesting the city's records ahead of time keeps a deal from stalling.

sections.h2: How does a house sale in Derby work?
sections.html:
Three routes exist: an agent listing, selling on your own, or a cash offer. Listing tends to mean repairs, showings and a buyer's lender, and a cash buyer skips the loan.

The deed is what transfers a house in Kansas. It goes to the Register of Deeds with a Real Estate Sales Validation Questionnaire, after which the County Clerk revises the tax record. Tax on a Derby parcel is billed by the Sedgwick County Treasurer, and you pay the whole amount or the first half by December 20 and the second half by May 10.

  • Get the Treasurer's current balance before choosing a closing date.
  • Ask the City of Derby or the County Clerk about special assessments.
  • Collect permit records for work done on the house.

Special assessments are easy to overlook. They are tracked apart from the general tax levy, so a clear tax balance does not mean none are attached to the parcel. Asking early lets you correct the payoff figure before a buyer or title company raises it. The same goes for open permits: the city permit office can tell you what is on record, and finishing or closing an old permit is far easier before an offer is on the table than during the final week before closing.

Summers in Derby run hot and humid, and winters are mild to cool. Hail and flood exposure are questions for a home inspection and your insurer.

Because the city's permit rules include a Flood Plain Development Permit, find out whether your lot sits in a mapped flood area instead of assuming nothing applies. The permit office at 788-6632 can answer questions about flood plain mapping for your address.

Valuation of Derby parcels belongs to the Sedgwick County Appraiser. Notices are mailed March 1. The informal appeal form must be back within 30 days, usually by March 31, and only one appeal per tax year is allowed.

When taxes fall behind, parcels reach foreclosure listing at two and a half or three and a half years of delinquency, and a $400 fee is added on October 1 of the listing year. Payment in full ends the case, and owners may redeem until the close of business the day before the auction.

A cash sale paying the balance at closing can clear the lien. Whoever handles your sale should request a fresh payoff from the Treasurer, 316-660-9000, before fixing the closing date.

sections.h2: Steps in a Derby cash sale
sections.html:
1. Send the address and describe the house, including anything unfinished or unpermitted.
  2. Look over the written offer and compare it with what a listing would net after repairs and showings.
  3. If you accept, a title company searches the title and asks the Treasurer for the tax payoff.
  4. Sign the deed and the sales validation questionnaire. The title company files them with the Register of Deeds.
  5. Taxes, liens and any mortgage are paid from the proceeds, and you receive the rest.

For a military household, the useful part is control of the date. For an heir, it is not having to stage or fix a house you may not live near. For an owner behind on tax, it is a payoff that ends the foreclosure risk.

sections.h2: What do Derby sellers commonly deal with?
sections.html:
• A short timeline because of a military move or a job change.
  • Unpermitted work that a buyer's inspector flags.
  • Delinquent property tax, which the county Treasurer can pursue through foreclosure after roughly two and a half years.
  • Inherited houses where the family prefers a fast sale with no staging or repairs.

If one of these sounds like you, send the address of your Derby house and we will walk through a cash offer and the closing steps.

A small folder speeds everything up. Nothing here is needed just to request an offer, yet it answers a buyer's first questions.

  • The deed or a recent tax statement showing the legal owner.
  • Permit records for additions, a new roof, a deck or a finished basement
  • Any notice from the county about delinquent tax or special assessments.
  • A note on who lives there now: you, a tenant or no one.

With those in hand, talk about timing and price gets specific.

faqs.q: How many people live in Derby, KS?
faqs.a: About 25,625 people lived there in 2020, and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 26,606.

faqs.q: Which school district covers Derby, Kansas?
faqs.a: Derby Public Schools, USD 260, serves the city, McConnell Air Force Base, the Oaklawn Improvement District and some southern Wichita neighborhoods.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace a roof in Derby?
faqs.a: A roof or siding replacement larger than 400 square feet does. Call 788-6632 to check your project.

faqs.q: When is property tax due on a Derby house?
faqs.a: The Sedgwick County Treasurer sends the bill. The full amount or first half is due December 20 and the second half May 10.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Derby house as-is for cash?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash offer is an alternative to listing, and the buyer may accept the house as it is. Share the address and we will outline the steps.
